chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muawiya ibn Maysara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the palm tree (yield) for two years. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'So the fresh dates (rutab) can be sold for this picking, and such and such a picking after it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) had sold the henna for such and such a harvest.'

key_terms.الرُّطْبَةُ: Fresh dates (dates at the rutab stage)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell palm dates or henna before they are fully harvested in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility in pre-Islamic and early Islamic commercial customs (urf) adopted by the Shia Imams, specifically validating the sale of future agricultural yields like palm dates and henna before full harvest. It underscores the principle that such transactions are permissible provided the quantity and quality are reasonably defined, reflecting the Imam's endorsement of his father's (Imam al-Sadiq's) established practice. This serves as a foundational text for contemporary Islamic finance models involving forward contracts and commodity trading.
